title: Missed punch detection
description: The system must detect shifts where an employee has a clock-in but no clock-out and flag them for correction.
rules: A shift with a clock-in and no clock-out after 16 hours is flagged as a missed punch.
The flagged shift is shown to the employee's manager for review.
The employee can submit a correction request with a proposed clock-out time.
A proposed clock-out time cannot be earlier than the clock-in time.

title: Daily overtime calculation
description: Hours worked beyond the daily threshold are calculated as overtime and paid at a higher rate.
rules: Hours over 8 in a single workday are classified as overtime.
Hours over 12 in a single workday are classified as double time.
Unpaid break time is excluded from worked hours.
Overtime is calculated per workday, using the employee's local time zone.

title: Weekly overtime risk alert
description: Managers are alerted when an employee is close to exceeding the weekly hours limit.
rules: An alert is raised when an employee's scheduled plus worked hours for the week reach 38 or more.
The alert is sent once per employee per week.
The alert is not sent for employees marked as exempt from overtime.

title: Leave request submission
description: Employees can request paid time off for future dates, subject to their available balance.
rules: A leave request must have a start date that is today or later.
The end date must not be before the start date.
A request is rejected if the requested days exceed the available balance.
Weekends and company holidays are not counted against the balance.
A request overlapping an existing approved leave is rejected.

title: Leave approval workflow
description: Managers approve or reject leave requests from their direct reports.
rules: Only the employee's direct manager can approve or reject the request.
A rejection requires a reason of at least 10 characters.
An approved request deducts days from the employee's balance immediately.
A request not actioned within 5 working days is escalated to the next-level manager.

title: Monthly leave accrual
description: Leave balance accrues each month based on length of service.
rules: Employees with under 2 years of service accrue 1.5 days per month.
Employees with 2 or more years of service accrue 2 days per month.
Accrual for a partial first month is prorated by days worked.
Balance is capped at 30 days; accrual stops at the cap.

title: Shift swap request
description: Two employees can swap shifts, with manager approval.
rules: Both employees must be qualified for the role on the swapped shift.
A swap must not cause either employee to exceed 48 scheduled hours in the week.
A swap must not leave less than 11 hours rest between consecutive shifts for either employee.
The swap takes effect only after the second employee accepts and the manager approves.

title: Schedule conflict detection
description: The system must prevent overlapping assignments for the same employee.
rules: An employee cannot be assigned two shifts that overlap in time.
An employee cannot be scheduled during approved leave.
A conflict is shown to the manager at the time of assignment, not after saving.

title: Timecard approval and lock
description: Timecards are approved by managers and locked before payroll runs.
rules: A manager can approve timecards only for their direct reports.
An approved timecard cannot be edited by the employee.
Timecards for a pay period are locked at payroll cutoff.
Edits to a locked timecard require payroll admin permission and are recorded in an audit log.

title: Handle overtime properly
description: The system should handle overtime properly for all employees.
rules: Overtime should be handled correctly.
Employees should be treated fairly.

title: Fast timecard approvals
description: Timecard approval should be quick and easy for managers.
rules: Approvals should happen in a reasonable time.
The approval screen should be user friendly.

title: Break compliance
description: Employees must take breaks as required by company policy and local law.
rules: Break violations should be flagged.
The system should follow all applicable rules.
